body:
§26 landed as-of on the data doors: any query, any past moment, no snapshots. The rendered
app route never got it — GET /:mount/app/:route resolves only the present. The cheapest large
demo payoff in the vision doc is blocked on exactly this: drag a date slider and watch the board
re-render as it stood last Tuesday, tickets blooming and shipping.

Build, in two halves:
1. The app doors accept ?asOf=<timestamp>. Route shape: appRouteOf (src/server/http.ts)
   requires exactly two segments — /:mount/app/<route>/<entity>. And "the app door" is TWO
   call sites — the public door and the full door both serve routes; thread asOf through
   serveRouteImpl once so BOTH doors honor it (criteria assert both; a one-door build leaves
   the other silently resolving the present).
   The render resolves its View the render resolves its View against the ground as
   of T, same lens, narrower delta-set — the §26 semantics, applied to the renderer's input. An
   invalid asOf refuses with the parameter named (door discipline). No asOf: byte-identical
   behavior to today.
2. demos/board grows the slider: a control in the rendered page that re-requests the route with
   asOf set. Keep it renderer-side and small — the door does the work.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A route rendered with asOf=T1 shows the value written before T1, not the later
    overwrite; the same route without asOf shows the latest (two-sided) — asserted on BOTH
    the public and the full door. Verify: new test test/server/app-asof.test.ts writing at
    two timestamps.
(b) An invalid asOf refuses with the parameter named and renders nothing. Verify: same file.
(c) An as-of window spanning an erasure carries the §26 annotation through to the rendered
    surface as SERVER-SIDE CHROME around the bundle's output (the §24.7 frameProbation
    precedent; §26: the annotation rides beside the view, never inside the resolved data —
    a payload field an unmodified bundle would ignore does not satisfy this) — the page will not silently pretend completeness. Verify: same file, erasure inside
    a mkdtemp fixture, two-sided (bystander content still renders).
(d) The board demo's rendered page contains the time control, and requesting the board route
    with an asOf shows a prior board state. Verify: extend test/board/board-render.test.ts (the rendered-route rail — it already
    fetches the app door over HTTP); a CDP browser pass is welcome if cheap but the HTTP
    rail is the criterion.

Merge tier: repair/extension of a landed promise (§26 said "on every door uniformly") —
self-merges on the ordinary bar.
title: As-of reaches the rendered route — and the board gets a time slider
